newsitem.title: UK: UK wheat futures bounce ahead of weekly tender.
newsitem.headline: UK wheat futures bounce ahead of weekly tender.

text.p: LIFFE wheat futures rallied in nervous trading on Wednesday ahead of the European Union's (EU) weekly grain tender, traders said.
"The market is worried about what the Commission will or more likely won't do at Thursday's tender," said a trader.
Traders said prices were now technically lower than those in the U.S. and export licences could be granted by the Commission without subsidies.
"Thursday is "D Day' - if Brussels doesn't grant a decent amount of exports this week, they never will," said a trader.
However, others said they doubted the Commission would do any thing to help the market on Thursday as it wants grain prices even lower.
"If we don't get a good result on Thursday prices will start to fall again and no-one can even guess where the bottom is," said another trader.
Wheat futures closed 0.50 to 0.75 stg up after trading 677 lots while barley was 0.25 stg down on a turnover of 65 lots.
In Amsterdam the milling wheat futures contract was neglected.
No business was reported on the UK fob market while delivered trade was said to be good.
Milling wheat 11 percent protein was fetching 120 stg a tonne for October on the south coast while 126 stg was paid for Jan/Mar in Liverpool.
Feed wheat in East Anglia was trading between 100.50 and 102 stg in the nearby positions while in the middle of the country 98.50 stg was paid for November and 99 stg for December.
Feed barley was not very active with 103 stg paid for November in Tilbury.
